subject.title: [Bug]: /context detail shows ~62k untracked provider/runtime overhead on fresh OpenAI Codex gpt-5.5 session

question: Should `/context detail` grow a provider-aware Codex ledger for token buckets, or should it keep the generic residual until live Codex semantics are proven?
rationale: The code can expose more buckets, but the correct user-facing distinction between cache, native thread state, hidden provider state, billing, and compaction pressure needs maintainer intent and live Codex evidence.

options.title: Add provider-aware ledger
options.body: Implement the ledger in `/context detail` with live Codex proof and tests distinguishing cached input, current context occupancy, known OpenClaw prompt sections, and unknown residual.

options.title: Document generic residual
options.body: Keep the current output shape and document that the residual is intentionally unknown provider/runtime state until Codex exposes stronger attribution.

options.title: Wait for live evidence
options.body: Leave the issue open without implementation until a maintainer or reporter provides a current-main Codex OAuth run identifying the residual source.

recommendation.title: Add provider-aware ledger
recommendation.body: Implement the ledger in `/context detail` with live Codex proof and tests distinguishing cached input, current context occupancy, known OpenClaw prompt sections, and unknown residual.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the original `/context` prompt breakdown and merged adjacent Codex usage accounting work, so he is the best available owner for the semantics decision.
